question_evidence_ledger.topic: β feeding above Sn/Sp vs final Pn/Pp, gamma competition, normalization
source_locators: Dimitriou 2021 PDF p. 17, Section III.D, Eq. (9)
Dimitriou 2021 PDF pp. 20, 35, Section IV.A, IV.E, Hauser-Feshbach competition vs sharp cut-off
question_evidence_ledger.core_distinction: β feeding populates states in an open quantum system where particle decay width Γ_n (or Γ_p) competes directly with electromagnetic cascade width Γ_γ. Near threshold (E ~ Sn, Sp), particle kinetic energy approaches zero, suppressing Γ_n by centrifugal barrier and Γ_p by Coulomb barrier, resulting in Γ_n/p << Γ_γ. Consequently, feeding above threshold does not guarantee particle emission.
question_evidence_ledger.continuous_integral_formula: P_n = \frac{1}{\lambda_{\text{tot}}} \int_{S_n}^{Q_\beta} S_\beta(E) f(Z', Q_\beta - E) \frac{\Gamma_n(E)}{\Gamma_n(E) + \Gamma_\gamma(E)} dE

question_evidence_ledger.topic: Single vs multi-neutron emission, Pn vs average neutron number, thresholds and cascade
source_locators: Dimitriou 2021 PDF p. 4, Section II.A, Eq. (1)
Dimitriou 2021 PDF p. 7, Section II.A.1, multi-neutron counting
Dimitriou 2021 PDF p. 18, Section III.D.4, sequential emission

definitions.P_0n: Probability of zero neutrons emitted (decay de-exciting purely by γ-rays to bound daughter states)
definitions.P_1n: Probability of exactly 1 neutron emitted (yielding residual A-1)
definitions.P_2n: Probability of exactly 2 neutrons emitted (yielding residual A-2)
definitions.average_neutron_multiplicity: \bar{\nu}_d = \langle n \rangle = \sum_{x \ge 1} x P_{xn} = P_{1n} + 2 P_{2n} + 3 P_{3n} + \dots

question_evidence_ledger.distinction_hazard: Counting only total neutrons per beta decay without multiplicity unfolding measures \bar{\nu}_d, not Pn. For exotic neutron-rich nuclei with sizable P2n (e.g., 11Li, 86Ga), \bar{\nu}_d > Pn; equating them distorts r-process network yields.
question_evidence_ledger.channel_thresholds_cascade: Threshold for 1n is S_1n; threshold for 2n is S_2n = S_1n(A) + S_1n(A-1). Emission proceeds via sequential two-step cascade: intermediate state at Ex > S_2n emits first neutron leaving (A-1) at E'x; if E'x > S_1n(A-1) and Γ_n^(2) >> Γ_γ^(2), a second neutron is emitted. Direct dineutron emission is negligible in medium-heavy nuclei.

question_evidence_ledger.topic: Q-value/mass uncertainties, Jπ selection rules, particle l, Coulomb barrier
source_locators: Dimitriou 2021 PDF p. 17, Section III.D, Qβn window
Taprogge 2014 PDF p. 3, col. 2, selection rules to ground vs isomeric state
question_evidence_ledger.mass_uncertainty_impact: Energy window Qβn = Qβ - Sn = ΔM(Z,A) - ΔM(Z+1,A-1) - M_n. Because Fermi integral scales as (Qβ - E)^5, a 200-500 keV mass error near the window top alters calculated Pn by factors of 2-10, and can misclassify whether a nucleus is a delayed particle emitter.
question_evidence_ledger.angular_momentum_parity: \vec{J}_i = \vec{J}_f + \vec{l} + \vec{s}, \pi_i = \pi_f (-1)^l. Parity strictly locks l to even or odd.
question_evidence_ledger.centrifugal_barrier: V_cf = \hbar^2 l(l+1)/(2\mu r^2). Transmission T_l(ε_n) ~ ε_n^(l + 1/2). For high ΔJ (e.g. Ji = 11/2- to Jf = 0+ requiring l=5), neutron emission to ground state is heavily suppressed, forcing decay to excited states or γ competition.
question_evidence_ledger.coulomb_barrier: For delayed protons, V_c = Z' e^2 / R creates a multi-MeV barrier. Gamow penetrability P ~ exp(-2πη) suppresses low-energy proton emission by orders of magnitude, imposing an effective threshold hundreds of keV to MeV above Sp.

question_evidence_ledger.topic: Allowed GT vs First-Forbidden feeding, finite Q window, seniority and K-isomers
source_locators: Dimitriou 2021 PDF pp. 28-29, Section IV.C.2, Figs. 13-14 (Sn isotopes %FF = 60-75%)
Dunlop 2016 PRC 93, 062801(R), 129Cd isomer (11/2-) vs ground state (3/2+)
Taprogge 2014 PRL 112, 132501, 131In (1/2-) isomer vs (9/2+) ground state
question_evidence_ledger.gt_vs_ff_competition: Gamow-Teller (ΔJ=0,±1, Δπ=no) Giant Resonance frequently lies near or above Qβ. First-Forbidden (ΔJ=0,±1,±2, Δπ=yes) transitions bridge opposite-parity shells across major gaps (N=50, 82, 126). In 133-140Sn, FF transitions contribute 60-75% of total decay; ignoring FF causes a factor of 4-5 overestimation of half-lives.
question_evidence_ledger.isomer_structural_fingerprints: Seniority isomers (e.g. 129Cd 11/2- vs 3/2+) have distinct configurations and decay via fast GT ν1h11/2 -> π1h9/2 to high-spin daughter states, whereas ground states populate low-spin states. In deformed nuclei, K-isomers suffer hindrance f_ν = (T1/2/T1/2^W)^(1/ν), blocking low-K feeding and redirecting decay to high-lying multi-quasiparticle states above Sn.

question_evidence_ledger.topic: Neutron efficiency, beta trigger/dead time, decay chain background, unobserved gamma feeding
source_locators: Dimitriou 2021 PDF pp. 5-7, Section II.A.1, Eqs. (2)-(3), energy-dependent efficiency
Dimitriou 2021 PDF p. 11, Section II.C.1, Pandemonium effect and TAGS vs HPGe
Dimitriou 2021 PDF pp. 6-7, moderation delay and triggerless DAQ
question_evidence_ledger.efficiency_systematics: Moderated 3He detectors drop in efficiency above 1-2 MeV. Assuming constant efficiency introduces severe systematic biases if the measured isotope spectrum differs from calibrators (87Br, 95Rb, 137I); Eq. (3) requires spectrum-weighted convolution <ε_n>.
question_evidence_ledger.timing_and_deadtime: Neutron thermalization in polyethylene requires hundreds of microseconds. Triggered event systems suffer extreme dead time and pileup; modern measurements require triggerless digital DAQ with nanosecond timestamps.
question_evidence_ledger.decay_chain_correction: Implanted precursor decays into radioactive daughters that may also be βn emitters. Accurate Pn extraction requires solving full Bateman equations with independently validated half-lives and isomer ratios.
question_evidence_ledger.pandemonium_bias: HPGe detectors miss fragmented weak γ-ray cascades at high level densities above Sn, artificially underestimating high-energy feeding. Data points from discrete γ-spectroscopy are not model-independent intensities without TAGS validation.

question_evidence_ledger.topic: Real nuclear case: 132,131Cd -> 131In, data to interpretation, counter-arguments, boundaries
source_locators: Dimitriou 2021 NDS 173, 144, Section IV.C.2, Table I
question_evidence_ledger.experimental_facts: RIKEN BigRIPS + WAS3ABi + EURICA observed a single 988 keV γ line in prompt coincidence with 132Cd (T1/2 = 97(10) ms) βn decay, and the same 988 keV line in 131Cd (T1/2 = 68(3) ms) direct β decay. 131In has known ground state (9/2+) and β-emitting isomer at 365(8) keV (1/2-).
question_evidence_ledger.author_interpretation: 988 keV γ assigned as de-exciting the 1353 keV second excited state in 131In to the 365 keV (1/2-) isomer. Based on systematics and Duflo-Zuker monopole model, the 1353 keV state was tentatively assigned Jπ = (3/2-), representing the π1p3/2 hole state relative to 132Sn. Authors extrapolated a complete loss of proton subshell closures at Z=38, 40 along N=82 and predicted a 2.5 MeV quenching of the N=82 neutron shell gap from Sn to Zr.
counter_arguments: Spin-parity ambiguity: experimental data cannot exclude Jπ = (5/2-) (π0f5/2 hole) or three-quasiparticle core-excited states; assignment is model-dependent.
Over-extrapolation of shell quenching: subsequent isomer spectroscopy in 128Pd (Watanabe 2013) demonstrated robust N=82 magicity, contradicting uniform catastrophic quenching.

Missing particle branch data: Taprogge 2014 only measured prompt γ-rays; absolute P1n and neutron energy spectrum were not measured, leaving unobserved direct feeding to 131In ground or other states unquantified.
question_evidence_ledger.transfer_conditions: Findings at spherical closed-shell edge (131In) cannot be transferred to deformed nuclei (A ~ 130 Xe, Ba, Ce) where quadrupole/triaxial deformation splits single-particle orbitals into Nilsson levels with strong Coriolis mixing.

validation_experiment_proposal.target_reaction: Beta-decay of 132Cd produced via in-flight fission of 238U
validation_experiment_proposal.instrumentation: BRIKEN 4π high-efficiency moderated 3He array combined with segmented HPGe clover detectors and fast plastic β-counters with triggerless digital DAQ
validation_experiment_proposal.measurable_quantities: Absolute P1n and P2n branching ratios, and β-n-γ triple coincidences
validation_experiment_proposal.falsification_criterion: If measured absolute P1n is significantly larger than absolute intensity of the 988 keV γ-ray (P1n >> Iγ(988)), it proves that β-delayed neutron emission predominantly feeds other states (such as the 9/2+ ground state or 1/2- isomer) directly without emitting the 988 keV photon, falsifying the assumption of exclusive selective feeding through the 1353 keV hole state.
